reason: The text (Genesis 41) presents Joseph as a model leader who embodies responsibility and accountability for the people's welfare. Joseph demonstrates this through: (1) providing wise counsel to Pharaoh about preparing for the coming famine; (2) taking responsibility for systematically collecting and storing grain during the seven years of plenty ('וַיִּקְבֹּ֞ץ אֶת־ כָּל־ אֹ֣כֶל'); (3) being appointed as administrator 'over all the land of Egypt' with full accountability to Pharaoh; (4) directly managing the distribution of grain to the people during the famine ('וַיִּפְתַּ֨ח יוֹסֵ֜ף אֶֽת־ כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֤ר בָּהֶם֙ וַיִּשְׁבֹּ֣ר לְמִצְרַ֔יִם'); and (5) ensuring 'the land will not be cut off by the famine.' The narrative shows Joseph taking full responsibility for Egypt's welfare during crisis, making decisions that affect all the people's actions and survival.
